cau_hoi: What is the highest mountain in Vietnam, known as the "Roof of Indochina"?
giai_thich: Fansipan is 3,143 m high, located in the Hoàng Liên Sơn mountain range, in the provinces of Lào Cai and Lai Châu. It is called the "Roof of Indochina" because it is the highest point in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia. Previously, it took several days to climb to the summit through dense forests, but since 2016, a cable car system has allowed visitors to reach near the peak in about 20 minutes.

cau_hoi: The land territory of Vietnam on the map is often compared to the shape of which letter?
giai_thich: Vietnam is wide in the north and south, narrow in the central region, and curves along the coastline, resembling the letter S. The length from north to south is about 1,650 km, while the narrowest point is only about 50 km. This shape causes the climate and landscapes between regions to be very different, from snow in the northern mountains to year-round sunshine in the south.

cau_hoi: Ha Long Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for nearly 2,000 limestone islands, belongs to which province?
giai_thich: Ha Long Bay covers about 1,550 km², with thousands of limestone islands rising from the blue water, many of which have beautiful caves like Sung Sot Cave and Thien Cung Cave. The name "Ha Long" means "descending dragon," associated with the legend of a dragon spitting pearls to form islands to fight invaders. Hai Phong has the Cat Ba archipelago nearby, which is also part of the heritage.

cau_hoi: Which river has reddish-brown water due to carrying a lot of silt and flows through the capital Hanoi?
giai_thich: The Hồng River originates from Yunnan province (China), flows into Vietnam at Lào Cai, and then empties into the sea. The river water is reddish because it carries a lot of red silt from the mountainous region. Thousands of years of silt deposition have created the fertile Hồng River delta, the cradle of rice civilization. People have built thousands of kilometers of dikes to prevent floods.

cau_hoi: Which city has the largest population in Vietnam?
giai_thich: Ho Chi Minh City is the largest economic center in the country. From July 1, 2025, the city will be expanded by merging with Bình Dương and Bà Rịa – Vũng Tàu provinces, bringing the population to about 14 million people. The city also includes the Con Dao Islands offshore. The old name Saigon is still commonly used by locals, especially for the central area.

cau_hoi: What do Vietnamese people call the sea located to the east and south of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The East Sea is a large sea of the Pacific Ocean, covering about 3.4 million km², surrounded by many countries such as Vietnam, China, the Philippines, and Malaysia. Vietnam has two archipelagos, Hoàng Sa and Trường Sa, in the East Sea. This is one of the busiest sea routes in the world, with many cargo ships passing through every day.

cau_hoi: What is the largest plain in Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Mekong Delta covers about 40,000 km², nearly three times larger than the Hồng River Delta. This is the largest rice-producing area in the country, accounting for more than half of the rice output and most of the rice exports. This region is also famous for its fruit orchards, shrimp and fish farming, and a dense network of rivers and canals, where people travel by boats.

cau_hoi: Which province is Da Lat, famous for its cool climate year-round and known as the "city of a thousand flowers," located in?
giai_thich: Da Lat is located on the Lâm Viên plateau, about 1,500 m above sea level. The higher you go, the cooler the air becomes, so even though it is near the equator, the average temperature here is only about 18°C. The French established Da Lat in the late 19th century as a resort, following the suggestion of Dr. Alexandre Yersin. Da Lat grows a lot of vegetables and flowers.

cau_hoi: On land, which country does Vietnam share the longest border with?
giai_thich: The Vietnam-Laos border is about 2,300 km long, running along the Trường Sơn mountain range, longer than the border with China (about 1,450 km) and Cambodia (about 1,100 km). Vietnam does not share a land border with Thailand. Many border gates like Lao Bảo and Cầu Treo connect the two countries, and the Vietnam-Laos friendship is considered special.

cau_hoi: What is the southernmost point on the land of Vietnam located?
giai_thich: Cà Mau Cape belongs to Cà Mau province, where there is a national coordinate marker and a symbol of a ship facing the sea. This is the only place on the mainland of Vietnam where you can watch the sunrise over the East Sea and sunset over the Gulf of Thailand. Mangrove forests and silt help this cape extend into the sea by several tens of meters each year.

cau_hoi: In southern Vietnam (such as Ho Chi Minh City), what seasons are typically divided in a year?
A: Four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter
D: Two seasons: rainy season and dry season
giai_thich: The South is close to the equator, so it is hot year-round, with no cold winter. The rainy season usually lasts from around May to November, when the southwest monsoon brings moisture from the sea, resulting in sudden downpours. The dry season lasts from December to April. In contrast, the North has a cold winter and experiences the four seasons more distinctly.

cau_hoi: The largest port city in the North, known as the 'city of red phoenix flowers', is which city?
giai_thich: Hai Phong has had a seaport since the late 19th century and serves as the gateway to the sea for the entire Northern region. Red phoenix flowers are planted throughout the streets and bloom vibrantly in the summer. From July 1, 2025, Hai Duong province will merge into Hai Phong, significantly expanding the city. Hai Phong's Lach Huyen deep-water port can accommodate very large container ships.

cau_hoi: What is the largest island in Vietnam?
giai_thich: Phu Quoc is about 575 km², located in the Gulf of Thailand, now belonging to An Giang province (formerly part of Kien Giang). The island is famous for its fish sauce, pepper, pearls, and beautiful beaches like Sao Beach. Phu Quoc is known as the 'Emerald Island'. In 2025, the island will become a special administrative region with its own governance.

cau_hoi: Which province does the Spratly Islands of Vietnam belong to?
giai_thich: The Spratly Islands consist of over 100 islands, rocks, and reefs located in the South China Sea, hundreds of kilometers from the mainland. Spratly Island is the administrative center, featuring schools, temples, and a meteorological station. The Paracel Islands belong to Da Nang city. The Vietnamese government has asserted sovereignty over these two archipelagos for many centuries.

cau_hoi: When entering Vietnam, the Mekong River splits into which two major branches?
B: Vam Co Dong and Vam Co Tay
giai_thich: The Tien and Hau Rivers flow parallel through the delta and empty into the sea through multiple mouths. The Vietnamese refer to this section of the Mekong River as the Cuu Long River, meaning 'nine dragons', because in the past, the river emptied into the sea through nine mouths. Nowadays, some mouths have been silted up or blocked. Can Tho city is located along the Hau River.

cau_hoi: The city of Hue, the former capital of the Nguyen dynasty, is located by which poetic river?
giai_thich: The Perfume River flows slowly and gently through the imperial city of Hue, with the Thien Mu Pagoda on a hill by the riverbank. The river's name is explained by the fact that during the flower season, the fragrant flowers from upstream fall into the water. From January 1, 2025, Hue will become a centrally governed city, alongside Hanoi, Hai Phong, Da Nang, Ho Chi Minh City, and Can Tho.

cau_hoi: Which region of Vietnam grows the most coffee, thanks to its fertile basalt soil?
giai_thich: Basalt soil formed from the lava of extinct volcanoes millions of years ago is very loose, retains water well, and is nutrient-rich. The Central Highlands produces most of Vietnam's coffee, helping the country rank second in the world for coffee exports, primarily robusta coffee. Buon Ma Thuot city is known as the 'coffee capital'.

cau_hoi: The Lung Cu Flagpole, near the northernmost point of Vietnam, now belongs to which province after the 2025 province reorganization?
giai_thich: Lung Cu is located on the Dong Van stone plateau, previously part of Ha Giang province. From July 1, 2025, Ha Giang will merge with Tuyen Quang to form a new Tuyen Quang province. The flag at Lung Cu Flagpole measures 54 m², symbolizing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. The true northernmost point is the Lung Cu peak, located a short distance north of the flagpole.

cau_hoi: What is the longest mountain range in Vietnam, running along the border with Laos and down to the Central Highlands?
giai_thich: The Truong Son Range is over 1,000 km long, divided into Northern and Southern Truong Son. The mountain range acts as the 'backbone' of Central Vietnam, blocking winds and creating weather differences between its two slopes. During the resistance against the Americans, the Truong Son Road (Ho Chi Minh Trail) ran along this mountain range to transport people and goods to the South.

cau_hoi: Hai Van Pass, known as the 'most majestic pass in the world', lies between which two cities?
giai_thich: The pass is about 20 km long, stretching over the Bach Ma range where the mountains meet the sea. The summit of the pass is often shrouded in mist, hence it is also called 'Cloud Pass'. From the pass, one can look down at Da Nang Bay and Lang Co Lagoon. In 2005, the Hai Van Tunnel, about 6.3 km long, was inaugurated, allowing vehicles to bypass the winding pass.

cau_hoi: Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng National Park, home to famous caves like Sơn Đoòng, is now located in which province?
giai_thich: Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng is one of the oldest and largest limestone mountain regions in Asia, recognized by UNESCO as a World Natural Heritage site. From July 1, 2025, Quang Binh province will merge with Quang Tri to form a new Quang Tri province, with the administrative center located in Dong Hoi. Phong Nha Cave has an underground river that allows boats to go deep into the mountain.

cau_hoi: Cái Răng Floating Market, where people buy and sell fruits and agricultural products right on boats, is located in which city?
giai_thich: The floating market operates from early morning on the Can Tho River. Each boat hangs a sign on a tall pole called a 'cây bẹo' so that customers can see from afar what the boat is selling, whether it's squash, sweet potatoes, or pineapples. In the riverine areas of the Mekong Delta, waterways were once the main means of transportation, leading to the establishment of floating markets. Can Tho is the largest city in the Mekong Delta.

cau_hoi: When does the northeast monsoon blow into northern Vietnam?
B: In winter, from November to April
D: In summer, from May to July
giai_thich: The northeast monsoon originates from the cold high-pressure area in Siberia (Asia), bringing cold air southward. When it arrives, temperatures can drop by 5 – 10°C in just one day. Early winter brings cold and dry winds, while late winter winds pass over the sea, making them more humid and causing drizzle. The Bach Ma mountain range blocks most of this cold wind from moving south.

cau_hoi: The terraced fields of Mu Cang Chai, one of the most famous landscapes in the northern mountains, are primarily created by which ethnic group?
giai_thich: The Hmong people have carved the mountainsides into terraced fields, leading water from streams to irrigate rice for generations. The rice harvest season is around September – October, when the mountainsides turn golden. Mu Cang Chai was formerly part of Yen Bai province and is now part of Lao Cai province after the two provinces merged in 2025. The terraced fields retain water and prevent soil erosion on the slopes.

cau_hoi: Where does the red basalt soil in the Central Highlands originate from?
B: Lava from volcanoes that erupted long ago
D: Beach sand blown in by the wind
giai_thich: Millions of years ago, many volcanoes in the Central Highlands erupted, and basalt lava covered vast plateaus. Over time, basalt rock weathered in the hot and humid climate into red soil rich in iron and aluminum. Today, old volcanic craters can still be seen, such as Biển Hồ in Pleiku, which is a lake located in an extinct volcanic crater.

cau_hoi: The Hoa Binh Hydropower Plant, a major hydropower project built with the help of the Soviet Union, is located on which river?
giai_thich: The plant was built from 1979 to 1994, at times employing tens of thousands of workers. The reservoir of the plant not only generates electricity but also helps reduce flooding for the Red River Delta and Hanoi. The Da River is the largest tributary of the Red River. The Da River also hosts the Son La hydropower plant, the largest hydropower plant in Southeast Asia.

cau_hoi: How long is Vietnam's mainland coastline approximately?
giai_thich: The coastline stretches from Mong Cai (Quang Ninh) in the north to Ha Tien in the southwest. Among the provinces and cities, most border the sea. The long coastline brings many benefits: seaports, fishing, aquaculture, salt production, and beach tourism. However, it also makes Vietnam vulnerable to storms and rising sea levels.

cau_hoi: When was Ha Long Bay first recognized by UNESCO as a World Natural Heritage site?
giai_thich: In 1994, the bay was recognized for its exceptional scenic beauty. In 2000, the bay was recognized for the second time for its geological and geomorphological values: the islands are the result of millions of years of rainwater and seawater dissolving limestone. In 2023, the heritage was expanded to 'Ha Long Bay – Cat Ba Archipelago', spanning two localities, Quang Ninh and Hai Phong.

cau_hoi: In spring in northern Vietnam, there are days when the walls and floors are soaked as if they are 'sweating'. What is this phenomenon called?
giai_thich: After cold spells, the walls and floors remain cold. When warm, humid air from the sea blows in, moisture condenses into water upon contact with cold surfaces, similar to condensation on the outside of a glass of ice water. Humidity can reach nearly 100%. On humid days, it is advisable to close the doors to limit the influx of moist air into the house.

cau_hoi: Huu Nghi Border Gate, an important international border gate on the Vietnam – China border, is located in which province?
giai_thich: Huu Nghi Border Gate (formerly known as Nam Quan Pass) is located on the main road from Hanoi to China. Lang Son is a province that has not changed its borders when the provinces were rearranged in 2025. The province is famous for its limestone mountains, Tam Thanh Cave, and specialties like star anise and roasted duck. Goods such as Vietnamese fruits are exported through here in large quantities.

cau_hoi: After the administrative units are rearranged from July 1, 2025, how many provinces and centrally-controlled cities will Vietnam have?
giai_thich: Previously, Vietnam had 63 provinces and cities. After the rearrangement, the country will have 28 provinces and 6 centrally-controlled cities. 11 provinces and cities remain unchanged, such as Hanoi, Hue, Lang Son, Thanh Hoa, and Nghe An; the rest will merge together. The district level will also be eliminated, leaving only two levels of local government: province and commune, making the administrative apparatus more streamlined.

cau_hoi: The Dong Van Stone Plateau, the first global geopark recognized by UNESCO in Vietnam (in 2010), is famous for what landscape?
A: White sandy hills by the sea
C: Layered gray limestone mountains where locals grow corn in rock crevices
giai_thich: Most of the land here consists of sharp cat-ear stones, with very little arable land, so locals carry soil into rock crevices to grow corn. Water is also scarce as rainwater quickly seeps through the limestone into the ground. The plateau also preserves many ancient fossils hundreds of millions of years old, indicating that this area was once underwater.

cau_hoi: Where is the westernmost point of Vietnam, where the borders of Vietnam, Laos, and China meet?
D: A Pa Chai, Dien Bien province
giai_thich: A Pa Chai is a high mountainous area with remote old forests, marked by milestone number 0 indicating the border junction. There is a saying here: "a rooster's crow can be heard by all three countries." The four extreme points on land in Vietnam are: the northernmost at Lung Cu, the southernmost at Dat Mui, the easternmost at Mui Doi, and the westernmost at A Pa Chai.

cau_hoi: The easternmost point on land in Vietnam is Mui Doi, located in which province?
giai_thich: Mui Doi (also known as Hon Dau) belongs to the Hon Gom peninsula, where the national coordinate milestone is located. The road to here is very difficult, requiring climbing over many large rocks and sand dunes. Mui Doi is often confused with Mui Dien (Mui Dai Lanh) to the north, which is known as the place to catch the earliest sunrise on land and has an ancient lighthouse.

cau_hoi: What is the longest river that flows entirely within Vietnam's territory (not originating from abroad)?
giai_thich: The Dong Nai River is about 580 km long, originating from the Lam Vien plateau (Lam Dong) and flowing to the Southeast region before emptying into the sea. The Red River, Da River, and Mekong River all originate from China. The Dong Nai River has the Tri An hydroelectric lake, which provides electricity and fresh water for the Ho Chi Minh City area.

cau_hoi: In which direction does the land area of Vietnam primarily extend?
giai_thich: The narrow and elongated territory in the north-south direction causes the climate to change distinctly: the North has a cold winter, while the South is warm year-round. Coastal provinces all face the East Sea to the east. In the southwest, the coastline turns towards the Gulf of Thailand, where one can watch the sunset over the sea, such as in Ha Tien or Phu Quoc.

cau_hoi: What is the narrowest point on the land of Vietnam, with a width of about 50 km from the Laos border to the sea, belonging to which former province?
B: Quang Binh (now part of Quang Tri)
giai_thich: The area near Dong Hoi city is where the country is "waist-thin", with only about 50 km from the Vietnam-Laos border to the coastline. Due to its narrowness, rivers here are short and steep, and heavy rains can quickly cause floods. In contrast, the widest area on land is in the northern provinces, reaching about 600 km in the east-west direction.

cau_hoi: Con Dao, an archipelago famous for sea turtles coming ashore to lay eggs, now belongs to which administrative unit?
C: Ho Chi Minh City (previously part of Ba Ria – Vung Tau)
giai_thich: From July 1, 2025, Ba Ria – Vung Tau province will merge into Ho Chi Minh City, and Con Dao will become a special zone under the city. Con Dao consists of 16 islands, with the largest being Con Son. Con Dao National Park is the place where green turtles lay the most eggs in Vietnam, with thousands of nests protected and hatched each year.

cau_hoi: In Central Vietnam, when do storms and floods usually occur the most?
giai_thich: The storm season in Vietnam usually lasts from June to November, and the storm landing position gradually shifts from north to south over time. Central Vietnam has a late rainy season in autumn – winter, so the months of September to November experience both storms and heavy rain. The short and steep rivers from the Truong Son mountains flowing to the sea cause floodwaters to rise very quickly, leading to severe flooding.

cau_hoi: Ba Den Mountain, known as the "roof of the South" because it is the highest in the area (about 986 m), is located in which province?
giai_thich: Amidst the flat plains, Ba Den Mountain stands out like an island, visible from afar. On the mountain, there is Ba Pagoda and a cable car system that takes visitors to the summit. The new Tay Ninh (including the old Long An province from 2025) has its administrative center in Tan An. The southern region is mainly flat, so such mountains are very rare.

cau_hoi: Where does the Red River originate before flowing into Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Red River is about 1,150 km long, but only about 500 km flows through Vietnamese territory. In China, this section of the river is called Yuan River. The river enters Vietnam in Lao Cai, and the upstream section in the country is also known as the Thao River. It receives water from two major tributaries, the Da River and the Lo River, before flowing through Hanoi.

cau_hoi: Son Doong Cave, the largest natural cave chamber in the world, was discovered by a local resident around 1990. Who was that person?
giai_thich: Mr. Ho Khanh was searching for agarwood in the forest when he accidentally found the cave entrance with cold air blowing out and the sound of rushing water. Many years later, he led an expedition team from England, led by Howard Limbert, back in 2009 for exploration. The cave is so large that it can contain an entire row of skyscrapers, with forests and clouds inside.

cau_hoi: Ky Cung River in Lang Son Province is famous for being a "reverse-flowing" river. What does that mean?
A: The river flows in a circle around the city
B: The river flows backward at night
D: The river flows north into China instead of east into the East Sea like most rivers in the North
giai_thich: Most rivers in Northern Vietnam flow from northwest to southeast and empty into the East Sea. The Ky Cung River, however, originates in Lang Son, flows through Lang Son city, and crosses the border into China, joining the West River system and emptying into the sea near Guangzhou. Ky Lua Bridge and Ky Lua Market are famous landmarks along this river.

cau_hoi: "Lao Wind" is a hot dry wind that often blows strongly at the beginning of summer in which region of Vietnam?
A: North Central (such as Nghe An, Ha Tinh, Quang Tri) and part of the Northwest
giai_thich: The southwest monsoon from the Bay of Bengal carries a lot of moisture, causing heavy rain on the western slopes of the Truong Son range in Laos. When crossing the mountains to the eastern slopes, the wind loses moisture and heats up quickly, becoming a hot dry wind that can push temperatures above 40°C. It is called Lao Wind because it blows from Laos. This phenomenon of dry hot wind after crossing the mountains is known as the foehn effect.

cau_hoi: The largest hydroelectric power plant in Southeast Asia (about 2,400 MW), inaugurated in 2012, is which plant?
giai_thich: Son La Hydropower is located on the Da River, built from 2005 and completed ahead of schedule. To build the reservoir, tens of thousands of households in Son La, Dien Bien, and Lai Chau had to relocate. The Da River has many consecutive hydropower plants like steps: Lai Chau upstream, Son La in the middle, and Hoa Binh downstream.

cau_hoi: The North Quang region (formerly Ha Giang, now Tuyen Quang Province) is called the "rain center" of Vietnam. Why?
A: The average annual rainfall is among the highest in the country, about 4,000 – 5,000 mm
giai_thich: North Quang is located on the windward slope of high mountain ranges like Tay Con Linh. The humid air is pushed up, cools down, and condenses into a lot of rain. The rainfall here is about two to three times that of Hanoi. In contrast to the "rain center" North Quang, Phan Rang region (formerly Ninh Thuan) receives only about 700 mm of rain each year, making it the driest area in the country.

cau_hoi: Which region has the driest climate in Vietnam, with sand dunes, cacti, and vineyards?
C: Former Ninh Thuan (now part of Khanh Hoa Province)
giai_thich: Ninh Thuan has the least rainfall in the country because it is located in a sheltered position: the Southern Truong Son range blocks the southwest wind in summer, while the coastline runs nearly parallel to the northeast wind direction in winter, so the wind causes little rain. The abundant sunshine and strong winds help this area develop wind power, solar power, and salt production. From 2025, Ninh Thuan will merge into Khanh Hoa Province.

cau_hoi: In 2014, the Trang An Scenic Landscape Complex (Ninh Binh) became Vietnam's first and Southeast Asia's first World Heritage site of which type?
giai_thich: Trang An features limestone mountain ranges, flooded valleys, and caves that run through the mountains, where visitors can take boats. Archaeologists have found traces of prehistoric people living in the caves for tens of thousands of years, along with the ancient capital Hoa Lu of the Dinh and Early Le dynasties. Therefore, UNESCO recognized Trang An for both its natural and cultural values.

cau_hoi: Ma Pi Leng Pass, considered the "king of all passes" in Vietnam, overlooks the deep gorge of which river?
giai_thich: The pass is about 20 km long, connecting Dong Van and Meo Vac on the stone plateau. "Ma Pi Leng" in the local language means "horse's nose ridge", because the road is so steep that even horses have to gasp for breath while passing. Below, the emerald Nho Que River flows through Tu San gorge, one of the deepest gorges in Southeast Asia, with cliffs rising about 700 – 900 m high.

cau_hoi: Ban Gioc Waterfall, one of the most beautiful waterfalls in Vietnam, is particularly notable for what?
A: The waterfall is located right on the Vietnam – China border
B: The waterfall is inside a cave
C: The waterfall flows upward to the sky
D: The waterfall only has water in winter
giai_thich: Ban Gioc Waterfall is located in Cao Bang Province, on the Quay Son River. The waterfall is about 300 m wide and over 50 m high, cascading through many limestone layers creating a white water curtain. Part of the waterfall belongs to Vietnam, and part belongs to China, making it one of the largest waterfalls in the world located on the border between the two countries.

cau_hoi: Which mountain range juts out to the sea between Hue and Da Nang, considered the climatic boundary between the cold winter of the North and the warm year-round South?
giai_thich: The Bạch Mã Range runs in an east-west direction, blocking most of the cold northeast monsoon winds from moving south. Therefore, the northern side of the Bạch Mã Range experiences a cold winter, while the southern side is warm year-round. The Hải Vân Pass crosses this mountain range. The Bạch Mã mountain area is also a national park and once had a French resort at its peak.

cau_hoi: Ba Bể Lake, the largest natural freshwater lake in the mountainous region of Vietnam, is now located in which province?
giai_thich: Ba Bể Lake is situated among limestone mountains and was formed when the river flow was blocked in the karst region millions of years ago. The lake is surrounded by a national park with pristine forests and many rare animal species. In 2011, the lake was recognized as a Ramsar site, a wetland of international importance. From 2025, Bắc Kạn will merge with Thái Nguyên.

cau_hoi: The famous red and white sand dunes, which change shape with the wind, near Mũi Né, belong to which province today?
giai_thich: Strong winds from the sea carry sand to form dunes, and the continuous wind causes the dunes to move and change shape, hence they are also called "flying sand dunes." The red color of the sand is due to high iron oxidation. From 2025, Bình Thuận will merge with Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông to form a new Lâm Đồng province, which will have both the high mountains of Đà Lạt and the sea.

cau_hoi: What is the world-famous feature of Cam Ranh Bay (Khánh Hòa)?
B: It is the bay with the most islands in the world
C: It is one of the best natural harbors in the world, deep and sheltered from the wind
giai_thich: Cam Ranh Bay is surrounded by a peninsula and mountain ranges, with a narrow entrance, making the waves inside very calm, and the deep water allows large ships to enter. Therefore, more than a hundred years ago, many foreign fleets stopped here. In 1905, the Russian fleet stopped at Cam Ranh on its way to the Tsushima naval battle with Japan.

cau_hoi: What is the first marine protected area of Vietnam, established in 2001, with rich coral reefs, located?
giai_thich: The Hòn Mun Marine Protected Area was established with the support of international organizations and is home to the most coral species in Vietnam. The island's name comes from the black color of the rocks here, resembling ebony. The protected area prohibits fishing in the core zone to allow corals and fish to recover. Nha Trang Bay is also a member of the "Club of the Most Beautiful Bays in the World."

cau_hoi: Which province has the largest coal reserves in Vietnam, known as the "black gold" region?
giai_thich: Most of Vietnam's coal is located in Quảng Ninh, primarily anthracite coal, which contains a lot of carbon and burns with high heat. Coal has been mined in Hòn Gai, Cẩm Phả, and Uông Bí since the French colonial period. Quảng Ninh miners are famous for their spirit of "discipline and unity." Coal is used for thermal power plants, cement, and export.

cau_hoi: The Bạch Hổ oil field offshore Vũng Tàu, where Vietnam's first tons of oil were extracted in 1986, is special for what reason?
A: The field is located under an island
B: Oil rises to the surface of the sea
D: Oil was found in granite bedrock, which was previously thought impossible
giai_thich: Typically, oil is found in sedimentary rocks like sandstone. At Bạch Hổ, Vietnamese and Soviet engineers discovered oil accumulating in the cracks of granite bedrock below. This discovery helped Bạch Hổ become the largest oil field in Vietnam and changed the global oil industry's perception of where oil could be found.

cau_hoi: What is notable about the Cái Mép – Thị Vải port complex in Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Bà Rịa – Vũng Tàu)?
A: It is only for cruise ships
C: It is a deep-water port that can accommodate very large container ships directly to Europe and America
D: It is the smallest river port in Vietnam
giai_thich: Before Cái Mép – Thị Vải, goods from the South often had to be transported by small ships to Singapore or Hong Kong to transfer to larger ships. Thanks to the deep water channel, the port can accommodate ships carrying over 20,000 containers. Cái Mép – Thị Vải is often ranked among the most efficient container ports in the world.

cau_hoi: In which year did Vietnam's population exceed 100 million people?
giai_thich: According to the General Statistics Office, Vietnam's population reached 100 million people in 2023, ranking third in Southeast Asia after Indonesia and the Philippines, and about fifteenth in the world. In 1945, Vietnam had only about 23 million people. A large population is a rich labor source, but the aging rate is increasing rapidly as people are having fewer children than before.

cau_hoi: How many officially recognized ethnic groups does Vietnam have?
giai_thich: The Kinh (Vietnamese) ethnic group makes up about 85% of the population, while 53 ethnic minorities mainly live in mountainous and highland areas. The largest among the ethnic minorities are the Tày, Thái, Mường, Khmer, and Mông. Each ethnic group has its own language, clothing, and festivals, such as the communal house of the Ba Na people, the stilt house of the Thái people, or the Chôl Chnăm Thmây festival of the Khmer.

cau_hoi: What is the terrain characteristic of Đồng Tháp Mười, a vast area in the Mekong Delta?
B: Low-lying area, flooded during the flood season, previously barren acidic land
giai_thich: Đồng Tháp Mười spans the old Long An, Đồng Tháp, and old Tiền Giang. During the flood season, the Mekong River overflows, making the entire area a vast expanse of water. Previously, this was acidic barren land with difficult farming conditions. Thanks to the construction of canals to bring fresh water to wash away the acidity, this area has now become a rice granary. Lotus flowers and cajuput forests are typical images of Đồng Tháp Mười.

cau_hoi: What is the largest natural lake in the inner city of Hanoi, covering about 500 hectares?
giai_thich: West Lake has a circumference of about 17 km, which is approximately 40 times larger than Hoàn Kiếm Lake. Geographers believe the lake was formed from an old bend of the Red River: when the river changed course, the bend was left behind as a lake. There is Trấn Quốc Pagoda by the lake, one of the oldest pagodas in Hanoi. Trúc Bạch Lake is located nearby, separated by Thanh Niên Street.

cau_hoi: "Indochina Junction", where the borders of Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia meet, now belongs to which province of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Indochina Junction milestone is located on a mountain in Bờ Y commune, Ngọc Hồi district (old). The milestone has three faces, each facing one country and engraved with that country's coat of arms. From 2025, Kon Tum province will merge with Quảng Ngãi to form a new Quảng Ngãi province, stretching from the Central Highlands mountains to the sea and Lý Sơn Island.

cau_hoi: How was Lý Sơn Island (Quảng Ngãi), famous for its garlic fields, formed?
D: From volcanic activity, with extinct craters still present
giai_thich: Lý Sơn has five extinct volcanic craters, black basalt rocks, and Câu Cave formed by sea waves eroding volcanic rock. Locals grow garlic on the white sand brought from the seabed covering the red basalt soil, giving Lý Sơn garlic a special flavor. Lý Sơn is also the homeland of the soldiers of the old Hoàng Sa team.

cau_hoi: The world biosphere reserve of Cù Lao Chàm (2009), with coral reefs and bird nests, is located near which ancient city?
giai_thich: Cù Lao Chàm consists of 8 small islands, about 15 km off the coast of Hội An. This was the first place in Vietnam to implement "saying no to plastic bags" to protect the marine environment. In the past, Cù Lao Chàm was a stopover for merchant ships on the porcelain route across the East Sea. From 2025, Hội An and Cù Lao Chàm will belong to Da Nang city.

cau_hoi: Ngũ Hành Sơn in Da Nang consists of five mountains named after the five elements (Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth). What type of rock are these mountains primarily made of?
giai_thich: Marble is limestone that has been transformed under high temperature and pressure deep within the earth, becoming harder and more beautiful with veins. These mountains were once islands offshore, later connected to the mainland by sediment and sand. The Non Nước stone carving village at the foot of the mountain is famous for its stone statue carving craft that has existed for hundreds of years.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the bridge in Da Nang shaped like a golden dragon, which breathes fire and water on weekends, spanning which river?
giai_thich: The Dragon Bridge is 666 m long, inaugurated in 2013 to commemorate the 38th anniversary of Da Nang's liberation. The dragon shape is inspired by the Ly dynasty dragon, winding towards the sea. Da Nang is famous as "the city of bridges" with the Hàn River swing bridge, Trần Thị Lý bridge, and Thuận Phước bridge. The Hàn River flows through the city center to Da Nang Bay.

cau_hoi: Which region in Vietnam is famous for its lychee, known for being exported to Japan, the USA, and Europe?
D: Bắc Giang (now part of Bắc Ninh province)
giai_thich: Lychee trees need a sufficiently cold winter to bloom, so they grow well in the North. The lychee harvest season is around June, bustling with traders. Besides Lục Ngạn, Thanh Hà lychee (old Hải Dương, now part of Hải Phòng) is also very famous. From 2025, Bắc Giang will merge with Bắc Ninh to form a new Bắc Ninh province.

cau_hoi: Which famous tea region in Vietnam is known as the "First Famous Tea"?
giai_thich: Tân Cương tea has small, curly leaves, a green-yellow color, and a mild astringent taste with a sweet aftertaste. The climate and soil of the hilly region of Thái Nguyên, along with traditional manual tea roasting methods, create a unique flavor. Thái Nguyên is one of the provinces with the largest tea area in the country. Vietnam is one of the largest tea-exporting countries in the world.

cau_hoi: In 2008, Hanoi was expanded approximately 3.6 times by merging with which province?
A: Hà Tây (along with a district of Vĩnh Phúc and four communes of Hòa Bình)
giai_thich: From August 1, 2008, the entire Hà Tây province, Mê Linh district (Vĩnh Phúc), and four communes of Hòa Bình were incorporated into Hanoi. The capital's area increased to about 3,300 km², placing it among the largest capitals in the world. The new Hanoi includes Ba Vì mountain, Hương pagoda, and the ancient village of Đường Lâm. In the 2025 reorganization, Hanoi will maintain its boundaries.

cau_hoi: Buckwheat flowers, the pink-purple flowers that cover the hills around October to November, are associated with which region?
D: Ha Giang Stone Plateau (now part of Tuyen Quang)
giai_thich: Buckwheat seeds are triangular in shape. In the past, the Mong and Lo Lo people grew them for food, making cakes and brewing alcohol. The flowers change color over time, from white to pink and then purple. Since becoming a tourist destination, they have been planted more for visitors to admire. The buckwheat flower festival is held annually in Ha Giang.

cau_hoi: Vietnam is the world's leading exporter of cashew nuts. Which region was once called the "cashew capital" of Vietnam?
C: Binh Phuoc (now part of Dong Nai Province)
giai_thich: The cashew tree originates from Brazil, is drought-resistant, and thrives in the basalt hills and gray soil of the Southeast. The cashew nut is found in a hard shell that grows outside, beneath the juicy "fruit" which is actually the swollen stem of the fruit. The shell contains an oil that can cause skin burns, so it must be processed carefully. From 2025, Binh Phuoc will merge with Dong Nai.

cau_hoi: Which fish is widely farmed in the Mekong Delta, helping Vietnam become a leading exporter of this type of fish?
giai_thich: Pangasius is a type of catfish that lives in the Mekong River, grows quickly, and is easy to farm in ponds and rafts. The fillet of pangasius is white, has few bones, and is exported to over 100 countries. The pangasius farming industry is concentrated in Dong Thap, An Giang, and Can Tho. The relative of pangasius is the giant pangasius, one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, which is now very rare.

cau_hoi: "Flood season" in the Mekong Delta, when floodwaters from the Mekong River overflow into the fields, usually occurs around which month?
giai_thich: Unlike the severe flash floods in the mountains, the water rises slowly, a few centimeters each day, so the locals call it "flood season" instead of flood season. The water carries silt that enriches the fields and washes away salinity. This is also the season for fish, lotus flowers, and water lilies. Recently, hydropower dams upstream have reduced the flood season and the amount of silt.

cau_hoi: O Quy Ho Pass, the longest pass in Vietnam (about 50 km), crosses which mountain range?
giai_thich: The pass connects Sa Pa (Lao Cai) with Tam Duong (Lai Chau), with the peak of the pass nearly 2,000 m high. The pass is also known as "Heaven's Gate" because clouds often cover the peak. The Hoang Lien Son Range blocks the northeast monsoon, resulting in different weather on either side of the pass: Sa Pa is cold and foggy, while Lai Chau is sunnier.

cau_hoi: The four passes known as the "Four Great Passes" in the northern mountainous region include Ma Pi Leng, O Quy Ho, Pha Din, and which pass?
giai_thich: Khau Pha Pass in Mu Cang Chai means "horn of heaven" in Thai, as the mountain peak seems to touch the sky. This place hosts a paragliding festival over the terraced fields during the rice harvest season. Pha Din Pass connects Son La and Dien Bien, once a difficult road for transporting people and supplies to the Dien Bien Phu battlefield in 1954.

cau_hoi: Hoa Binh, Son La, and Lai Chau hydropower plants are all located on the Da River. Where does the Da River originate?
giai_thich: The Da River is about 900 km long, flowing in a northwest-southeast direction through the Northwest mountainous region, between the Hoang Lien Son Range and the limestone plateaus. The river has many rapids and a strong flow, making it the largest source of hydropower in Vietnam. In China, the river is called Li Jian. The Da River flows into the Red River in the Viet Tri – Ba Vi area.

cau_hoi: Lang Biang, a mountain about 2,167 m high in Da Lat, is associated with the love legend of which ethnic couple?
giai_thich: According to legend, K'Lang and H'Biang loved each other but were forbidden to be together due to their different tribes. She died while blocking an arrow for him, and he died of grief, and the two became mountains. Their tears formed the Da Nhim stream. From the peak of Lang Biang, one can overlook Da Lat and the Golden Stream Lake.

cau_hoi: Moc Chau Plateau (Son La), with its green tea hills and dairy farms, is famous for which type of flower that blooms white in spring?
giai_thich: Moc Chau is about 1,000 m high, with a cool climate and vast pastures, making it very suitable for dairy farming. In spring, the plum orchards bloom white, along with fields of white mustard flowers, creating a scene reminiscent of snow. In recent years, Moc Chau has become a famous tourist destination in the Northwest with its heart-shaped tea hills and Bach Long glass bridge.

cau_hoi: The mountain ranges in northeastern Vietnam (Song Gam, Ngan Son, Bac Son, Dong Trieu) have what special shape?
C: Arc shape, expanding to the north and northeast, converging at Tam Dao
giai_thich: The arc-shaped mountain ranges resemble the ribs of a fan opening to the north. This shape creates "corridors" that allow the northeast monsoon to penetrate deeply, making the Northeast the coldest winter region in the country. In contrast, the mountain ranges in the Northwest, such as Hoang Lien Son, run northwest-southeast, blocking some of the cold winds.

cau_hoi: The Duong River, famous from the poem "On the Other Side of the Duong River" by Hoang Cam, connects which two river systems?
B: Mekong River and Dong Nai River
C: Red River and Thai Binh River
giai_thich: The Duong River branches off from the Red River in Hanoi, flows through the Kinh Bac region, and then merges into the Thai Binh River near Phả Lại. During the flood season, the Duong River transfers some of the Red River's water to the Thai Binh River, reducing flooding for Hanoi. Dong Ho painting village and Phu Lang pottery village are located along the banks of the Duong River.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the first urban railway line in Vietnam, which became operational in 2021?
D: Ben Thanh – Suoi Tien (Ho Chi Minh City)
giai_thich: The Cat Linh – Ha Dong line is about 13 km long, elevated, with 12 stations, inaugurated in November 2021. By December 2024, Ho Chi Minh City will launch metro line No. 1 Ben Thanh – Suoi Tien, the city's first metro line. Urban railways help reduce traffic congestion and air pollution in major cities.

cau_hoi: How long is the North-South railway line (Thống Nhất) connecting Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City?
giai_thich: The railway line is approximately 1,726 km long, completed by the French in 1936. During the war, the line was divided and heavily damaged. In 1976, the first Thống Nhất train ran continuously from North to South, taking nearly 3 days. Today, the journey takes about 30 – 35 hours. The section through Hai Van Pass is considered one of the most beautiful railway routes in the world.

cau_hoi: What weather phenomenon is Mount Mau Son in Lang Son famous for during severe cold spells in winter?
giai_thich: Mount Mau Son has an elevation of about 1,500 m, located in the Northeast region, where the northeast monsoon is strongest. When temperatures drop below 0°C, moisture freezes on plants, roofs, and occasionally snow falls. The French once built vacation villas on the mountain. Whenever there is news of frost and snow, many tourists flock to Mau Son and Sa Pa to admire the scenery.

cau_hoi: Cao Phong orange, a famous sweet orange variety from the North, is grown in which former province, now part of Phu Tho province?
giai_thich: As of 2025, Phu Tho province was formed from three provinces: Phu Tho, Vinh Phuc, and Hoa Binh, with the administrative center in Viet Tri. Cao Phong oranges have been cultivated in the low mountainous region of Hoa Binh since the 1960s. Nghe An is also famous for Vinh oranges, while Ha Giang has green oranges. Hung Yen is known for its longan.

cau_hoi: Hòa Lộc mango, a famous mango variety considered by many to be the best in Vietnam, originates from where?
C: Old Tien Giang (now part of Dong Thap)
giai_thich: Hòa Lộc mango has large fruit, golden, smooth flesh, low fiber, and is very fragrant and sweet. This variety is grown in Hòa Lộc commune, former Cai Be district. From 2025, Tien Giang will merge with Dong Thap to form the new Dong Thap province, with the administrative center in My Tho. The Mekong Delta is the largest fruit-growing area in the country.

cau_hoi: What rank does Vietnam hold in the world for pepper exports?
giai_thich: Vietnam accounts for about half of the world's pepper export volume. Pepper is widely grown in the Central Highlands, Southeast region, and Phu Quoc island. The pepper plant is a climbing vine, with fruits growing in clusters; black pepper is the dried fruit with the skin on, while white pepper is the seed that has been peeled. In the past, pepper was as valuable as gold and was a driving force behind European exploration.

cau_hoi: Rubber trees, an industrial crop for latex used in making tires, are most commonly grown in which region of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Southeast region has gray soil and basalt red soil, a hot climate year-round, few storms, making it very suitable for rubber trees. The French established large rubber plantations from the early 20th century. The rubber tree originates from the Amazon rainforest in South America. People make a slanted cut on the tree's bark to collect the white latex that flows into a collecting cup.

cau_hoi: The Tam Coc – Bich Dong tourist area in Ninh Binh is often referred to as what due to its limestone mountains and waterways?
giai_thich: Tam Coc means "three caves," as visitors take a boat on the Ngo Dong River through three caves that pass through the mountains: Ca Cave, Hai Cave, and Ba Cave. On both banks are rice fields and steep limestone mountains, resembling the rocky islands of Ha Long Bay but in the middle of the plain. As of 2025, Ninh Binh will also include the former provinces of Ha Nam and Nam Dinh.

cau_hoi: According to folklore, "ngau rain" often appears in the North around the seventh lunar month, associated with which legend?
D: Ngưu Lang – Chức Nữ meeting over the Ô Thước bridge
giai_thich: The story says that Ngưu Lang and Chức Nữ can only meet once a year on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month, and their tears fall to the earth as ngau rain. Scientifically, this is the middle of the rainy season, with small rain spells lasting several days due to the tropical convergence zone operating in the North. Ngau rain is persistent but usually not heavy.

cau_hoi: The Golden Bridge in Ba Na (Da Nang), famous worldwide since 2018, has what special feature?
A: The longest bridge in the world
B: A bridge floating on the sea
C: A yellow pedestrian bridge supported by two giant stone hands
D: A bridge made of real gold
giai_thich: The Golden Bridge is about 150 m long, located at an altitude of about 1,400 m on Ba Na Mountain. The giant hands, which look like they are made of mossy stone, are actually made of steel frames and fiberglass mesh. Ba Na is a resort area built by the French since 1919 due to its cool climate, with temperatures often 8-10°C lower than in the plains.

cau_hoi: As of 2025, the tallest building in Vietnam, approximately 461 m high, is located in which city?
giai_thich: Landmark 81 has 81 floors above ground, inaugurated in 2018, located by the Saigon River. The design is inspired by a bundle of bamboo, symbolizing the spirit of Vietnamese solidarity. Previously, the tallest building was Keangnam Landmark 72 in Hanoi (about 336 m). Landmark 81 is among the tallest buildings in Southeast Asia.

cau_hoi: Sam Son Beach, one of the most famous resorts in the North since the French colonial period, belongs to which province?
giai_thich: The French began building vacation villas in Sam Son in the early 20th century due to its long, gentle sandy beach and clear water. Here, there is Mount Truong Le with the Doc Cuoc Temple and the famous Trống Mái rock. Thanh Hoa is a populous province with the largest plain in Central Vietnam, maintaining its boundaries in the 2025 reorganization.

cau_hoi: Tra Su Melaleuca Forest, a famous wetland forest with paths covered in green duckweed, is located in which province?
giai_thich: Tra Su Melaleuca Forest is located in the Bay Nui region, near the Cambodian border. During the flooding season, visitors can row boats through the rows of melaleuca trees, with the water surface covered in green duckweed like a carpet. The forest is home to many bird species such as herons, egrets, and cormorants. From 2025, An Giang will include the old Kien Giang with its administrative center in Rach Gia.

cau_hoi: The Trống Mái rock, two stones stacked on top of each other resembling a rooster and hen, is a symbol of which bay?
giai_thich: The Trống Mái rock (also known as the Fighting Cock rock) is about 10 m high, with a very small base, making it look like it is about to topple. This is the result of millions of years of sea waves and rainwater eroding the limestone at the foot of the island. The Trống Mái rock is one of the most familiar images on postcards and pictures of Ha Long. There is also another famous Trống Mái rock in Sam Son (Thanh Hoa).

cau_hoi: Thac Ba Lake, one of the largest artificial lakes in Vietnam, was created in 1971 when which hydropower plant was built?
A: The first hydropower plant in the North, on the Chảy River
giai_thich: Thac Ba Hydropower Plant is the first large hydropower plant in the North, built during wartime. The reservoir covers about 23,000 ha, with more than 1,300 large and small islands, which were hilltops before being submerged. The lake belongs to the old Yen Bai province, now part of Lao Cai province. The lake helps regulate floods for the Chảy and Lô rivers.

cau_hoi: Which region of Vietnam has the highest population density?
giai_thich: The Red River Delta has a long history of cultivation, with fertile alluvial soil suitable for multiple rice crops, leading to a high population concentration, with an average density of over 1,000 people/km². Hanoi is located in the center of the region. In contrast, the Northwest and Central Highlands have low densities due to high mountainous terrain and difficult transportation, despite having many resources.

cau_hoi: Mường Thanh Valley, the largest basin in the Northwest, where the historic battle of 1954 took place, belongs to which province?
giai_thich: Dien Bien basin is about 20 km long and 6 km wide, surrounded by hills. The flat land and the Nậm Rốm River flowing through make it a major rice-growing area in the Northwest, famous for Dien Bien rice. The French chose this location to build a fortified group because they thought they could control it from the surrounding hills, but those very hills became the place where Vietnamese troops set up artillery.

cau_hoi: The Tam Giang – Cau Hai lagoon system, considered the largest lagoon system in Southeast Asia, is located in which city?
giai_thich: The lagoon system is about 70 km long and covers about 22,000 ha, separated from the sea by long sandbanks, and opens to the sea through Thuan An and Tu Hien estuaries. The water in the lagoon is brackish, a mix of Huong River water and seawater. Thousands of fishing households rely on fishing and shrimp farming in the lagoon.

cau_hoi: Ben Tre, a region famous as the 'land of coconuts', has merged into which province since 2025?
giai_thich: Vinh Long province was newly formed from the three provinces of Vinh Long, Ben Tre, and Tra Vinh, located between the Tien and Hau rivers. Ben Tre has a lot of coconuts, with coconut candy and handicrafts made from coconut shells and fibers. Ben Tre consists of three large islets: An Hoa, Bao, and Minh, formed by the alluvium of the branches of the Tien River.

cau_hoi: Nam Định province, the homeland of the Trần dynasty, will belong to which province in 2025?
giai_thich: Ninh Bình province was newly formed from three provinces: Ninh Bình, Hà Nam, and Nam Định. The new province features limestone mountains of Tràng An, rice paddies, and a coastline with Kim Sơn beach and Xuân Thủy National Park. Nam Định is famous for its weaving craft dating back to the French colonial period and the Trần temple, where the spring opening ceremony takes place.

cau_hoi: The ancient town of Hội An and the Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, two world cultural heritage sites, will belong to which administrative unit in 2025?
giai_thich: From July 1, 2025, Quảng Nam province will merge with Da Nang City. As a result, Da Nang will have two world cultural heritage sites and will stretch from the sea to the Trường Sơn mountains bordering Laos. The new city will also feature Ngọc Linh mountain, the homeland of Ngọc Linh ginseng, and Cù Lao Chàm island.

cau_hoi: Sóc Trăng, a province with a large Khmer population and famous for Dơi Pagoda, will merge into which unit in 2025?
giai_thich: Cần Thơ City was newly formed from Cần Thơ, Hậu Giang, and Sóc Trăng. Thanks to Sóc Trăng, Cần Thơ now has a coastline. Dơi Pagoda is an ancient Khmer pagoda where thousands of bats hang from trees in the temple grounds. The Khmer boat racing festival in Sóc Trăng is one of the largest water festivals in the Mekong Delta.

cau_hoi: Cà Ná salt field, one of the largest salt fields in Vietnam, is located in an area with what kind of climate?
C: Lots of sunshine, strong winds, and very little rain
giai_thich: Cà Ná belongs to the old Ninh Thuận province (now Khánh Hòa), the driest region in the country. Seawater is channeled into salt fields, and the sun and wind cause the water to evaporate, leaving behind white salt crystals. The main salt-making season is during the dry season when there can be continuous sunshine for many days. Strong winds help the water evaporate faster, allowing the salt to crystallize quickly.

cau_hoi: In the languages of many ethnic groups in the Central Highlands, what does the word "Đắk" (or "Đạ", "Ea") mean in place names like Đắk Lắk, Đạ Huoai, Ea Súp?
giai_thich: Many place names in the Central Highlands are associated with water sources, as water is the most precious resource for the life of the villages. "Đắk Lắk" can be understood as "lake of water," associated with Lắk lake, a large natural freshwater lake in this province. Similarly, "Kon" means village, so Kon Tum is "village by the lake." The term "Plei" (as in Pleiku) also means village.

cau_hoi: Pongour Waterfall, awarded the title "Nam thiên đệ nhất thác" by King Bảo Đại, is located in which province?
giai_thich: Pongour Waterfall is located on the Đa Nhim River, cascading down through many wide basalt steps, resembling a giant staircase. In the rainy season, the waterfall is over 100 meters wide, with water spraying white foam. In the dry season, the stone steps are exposed, allowing visitors to walk on them. Lâm Đồng has many beautiful waterfalls like Datanla, Prenn, Voi, and Liên Khương, as the basalt plateau is carved into steps by rivers and streams.

cau_hoi: Mỹ Thuận Bridge, inaugurated in 2000 with assistance from Australia, has what special significance?
A: It is the first cable-stayed bridge across the Mekong River in Vietnam, connecting the old Tiền Giang with Vĩnh Long
C: It is a bridge connecting Vietnam with Cambodia
D: It is the longest bridge in the world
giai_thich: Previously, people and vehicles wanting to cross the Tiền River had to wait for a ferry, sometimes taking hours during holidays. Mỹ Thuận Bridge is about 1.5 km long, with cables radiating from two tall towers. Following this was Cần Thơ Bridge (2010) across the Hậu River, and Mỹ Thuận 2 Bridge (2023) parallel to the old bridge, connecting the expressway to the Mekong Delta.

cau_hoi: Thủ Thiêm Tunnel in Ho Chi Minh City, opened in 2011, has what special feature?
A: It is the longest mountain tunnel in the world
B: It is a tunnel under the sea connecting to Côn Đảo
C: It is the first road tunnel crossing a river in Vietnam, going under the Sài Gòn River
D: It is a tunnel for trains
giai_thich: Thủ Thiêm Tunnel was constructed using the "immersed tunnel" method: large concrete tunnel segments were precast on land, floated out to the river, and then submerged to connect with each other. The tunnel is about 1.5 km long, with approximately 370 m located under the river. It connects the city center with the new urban area of Thủ Thiêm on the eastern bank of the Sài Gòn River.

cau_hoi: Điện Cape (Mũi Đại Lãnh), considered the place to welcome the earliest sunrise on land in Vietnam, now belongs to which province?
giai_thich: From 2025, Phú Yên will merge with Đắk Lắk, so the new Đắk Lắk province will have both a coffee plateau and a coastline. Điện Cape has a lighthouse built by the French in 1890. The French called this cape Cap Varella. It is important to distinguish: the actual easternmost point on land is Mũi Đôi in Khánh Hòa.

cau_hoi: The new Gia Lai province (after merging with Bình Định in 2025) will have its administrative center in which city?
giai_thich: This is special: a province that was entirely on the plateau now has its administrative center in a coastal city. The new Gia Lai province stretches from the Cambodia border through the Pleiku plateau, down the An Khê pass to the sea in Quy Nhơn. Tây Sơn, the homeland of the brothers Nguyễn Nhạc, Nguyễn Huệ, and Nguyễn Lữ, is now also part of Gia Lai province.

cau_hoi: In which year was the Non Nuoc Cao Bang Global Geopark recognized by UNESCO?
giai_thich: Non Nuoc Cao Bang features limestone mountains, caves, Ban Gioc waterfall, Thang Hen lake, and rock layers that preserve traces of ancient seas dating back hundreds of millions of years. The global geopark is a site of special geological heritage, preserved in conjunction with tourism and community development. Previously, Vietnam had the Dong Van Stone Plateau (2010), followed by Dak Nong (2020).

cau_hoi: What rank does the South China Sea hold among the largest coastal seas of the Pacific?
giai_thich: The South China Sea covers approximately 3.4 million km², stretching from the Taiwan Strait to the Malacca Strait, where ships travel from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. The sea has two major bays adjacent to Vietnam: the Gulf of Tonkin and the Gulf of Thailand. The deepest point of the South China Sea is over 5,000 m deep. The sea is rich in oil, seafood, and coral reefs.

cau_hoi: According to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea in 1982, how wide is the territorial sea of a coastal state measured from the baseline?
giai_thich: The territorial sea is considered as territory over the sea, where the state has full sovereignty. Foreign ships may pass through without causing harm. Beyond that is the contiguous zone (up to 24 nautical miles) and the exclusive economic zone (up to 200 nautical miles), where the state has rights to exploit resources. One nautical mile is approximately 1,852 m, commonly used in maritime contexts.

cau_hoi: Among the 53 ethnic minorities in Vietnam, which one has the largest population?
giai_thich: The Tay people number nearly 2 million, primarily living in the Northeast region such as Cao Bang, Lang Son, and Tuyen Quang. They have stilt houses, perform then singing with traditional instruments, and are known for weaving brocade. Other populous ethnic groups include Thai, Muong, Mong, and Khmer. The then singing of the Tay, Nung, and Thai was recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage in 2019.

cau_hoi: Many areas in the Mekong Delta, such as Dong Thap Muoi and the Long Xuyen Quadrangle, were once abandoned due to which type of soil?
giai_thich: Acid sulfate soil forms in coastal lowlands where plant remains contain high sulfur content. When dry, the substances in the soil convert to acid, causing the water to turn yellow-red and taste sour, making it difficult for rice to grow. Locals dig canals to bring in fresh water to wash the acid sulfate soil, and scientists have bred rice varieties that can withstand this soil, turning barren land into rice granaries.

cau_hoi: What does the name "Hanoi", given by Emperor Minh Mang in 1831, mean?
giai_thich: "Ha" means river, and "Noi" means inside. This land is surrounded by the Red River (Nhi Ha) and the Day and To Lich rivers. Previously, the city had many names such as Dai La, Thang Long (during the Ly dynasty), Dong Do, and Dong Kinh. During the Nguyen dynasty, the capital moved to Hue, so the name Thang Long was changed to no longer signify a capital.

cau_hoi: What significance does the Long Bien Bridge, inaugurated in 1902 during French colonial rule, hold for Hanoi?
A: It is the first steel bridge across the Red River
B: It is currently the longest suspension bridge in Asia
D: It is a bridge exclusively for cars
giai_thich: The bridge is about 2.3 km long including access roads, originally named Governor Doumer, and was among the longest bridges in Asia at that time. The bridge was bombed multiple times during the war but was still repaired for continued use. Today, the bridge is only for trains, motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians, becoming a symbol of Hanoi.

cau_hoi: My Khe Beach in Da Nang was once listed by Forbes magazine (USA) in 2005 as what?
A: The coldest beaches in the world
B: The beaches with the most sharks
C: The most attractive beaches on the planet
D: The most beautiful black sand beaches
giai_thich: My Khe has a long stretch of fine white sand, gentle waves, clear water, and is close to the city center. During the war, American soldiers referred to this beach as "China Beach". From 2025, Da Nang will include Quang Nam, adding many beautiful beaches like Cua Dai, An Bang in Hoi An, and Tam Thanh with its mural village.

cau_hoi: Approximately what portion of Vietnam's land territory is mountainous?
giai_thich: Mountains occupy about 3/4 of the area, but mainly consist of low hills: land above 1,000 m accounts for about 85%. Mountains over 2,000 m only make up about 1%, concentrated in the Hoang Lien Son range. The plains only account for about 1/4 of the area but are home to most of the population and rice fields.

cau_hoi: What is the approximate area of Vietnam's land territory?
giai_thich: Vietnam has a land area of about 331,000 km², ranking approximately 65th in the world, close to Japan, Germany, or Norway. However, Vietnam's maritime area is about 1 million km², three times that of the land. Therefore, Vietnam is considered a maritime nation, with significant potential for seafood, oil, tourism, and transportation.

cau_hoi: Which province raises the most shrimp in Vietnam, known as the "shrimp capital"?
giai_thich: Ca Mau has many brackish shrimp ponds, along with shrimp farming models under mangrove canopies, preserving forests while generating income. Black tiger shrimp and whiteleg shrimp are key export products of Vietnam. From 2025, Bac Lieu will merge with Ca Mau, making Ca Mau an even larger shrimp farming area in the country, with coastal wind farms.

cau_hoi: Vietnam often ranks among the top few largest rice-exporting countries in the world. Which group does it belong to?
A: The top 3 countries, along with India and Thailand
giai_thich: In 1988, Vietnam had to import rice due to food shortages. Just a year later, thanks to the policy of land allocation to farmers, Vietnam began to export rice. To date, Vietnam exports about 7 – 9 million tons of rice annually to the Philippines, Indonesia, Africa, and many other places. Most of the exported rice comes from the Mekong Delta.

cau_hoi: National Route 1, the road running along the length of the country, starts from Huu Nghi border gate (Lang Son) and ends where?
giai_thich: National Route 1 is about 2,300 km long, passing through most provinces and cities, and was once the most important road connecting North and South. The route dates back to the feudal era and was called the "heavenly road." Today, the North-South Eastern Expressway is being built parallel to it, allowing for faster travel and reducing the load on National Route 1.

cau_hoi: Ba Vi Mountain in the west of Hanoi, associated with the legend of the mountain god Tan Vien, is the place of which deity in folklore?
giai_thich: Ba Vi Mountain has three main peaks, the highest being King Peak (about 1,296 m), which looks like an umbrella from afar, hence also called Tan Mountain (tan means umbrella). The legend of Son Tinh – Thuy Tinh explains the annual floods in the Red River Delta. The French once built a resort on the mountain. Today, it is Ba Vi National Park.

cau_hoi: Tam Dao town, a mountain resort built by the French in the early 20th century, has what kind of climate compared to Hanoi in summer?
A: Much cooler because it is at an altitude of nearly 900 m
C: Hotter because it is closer to the Sun
giai_thich: For every 100 m increase in altitude, the temperature drops by about 0.6°C. At an altitude of about 900 m, Tam Dao is about 5 – 6°C cooler than Hanoi. Therefore, the French built mountain resorts like Tam Dao, Sa Pa, Ba Na, Bach Ma, and Da Lat. Tam Dao used to belong to Vinh Phuc, now part of Phu Tho province.

cau_hoi: People often say Sa Pa has "four seasons in one day." What does that mean?
D: Morning is cool like spring, noon is sunny like summer, afternoon is chilly like autumn, and night is cold like winter
giai_thich: Sa Pa is at an altitude of about 1,500 – 1,600 m, with thin air that retains heat poorly. During the day, the sun heats up quickly, and at night, the heat dissipates quickly, causing a large temperature difference between day and night. In winter, Sa Pa sometimes experiences frost and snow. Sa Pa lies at the foot of the Hoang Lien Son mountain range, near Fansipan peak.

cau_hoi: The rice harvest in the Mekong Delta often has up to three crops a year. What allows this region to grow so many crops?
A: The soil is all sand, making it easy to plow
B: The climate is warm year-round, with abundant irrigation water and alluvial soil
C: There is melting snow providing water
giai_thich: In the South, there is no cold winter, so rice can grow year-round if there is enough water. The irrigation system channels water from the Tien River and Hau River into the fields, and short-duration rice varieties take only about 90 – 100 days. The three common rice crops are the Winter-Spring crop, Summer-Autumn crop, and Autumn-Winter crop. Continuous planting can also deplete the soil if not replenished with alluvium.

cau_hoi: The famous traditional fish sauce specialty of Vietnam, such as Phu Quoc and Phan Thiet, is mainly made from which type of fish?
giai_thich: Anchovies are small, high in protein, and are caught abundantly in the central coastal region and the Gulf of Thailand. The fish are salted in large wooden barrels for several months. Phu Quoc fish sauce was the first product from Vietnam to be protected by the European Union's geographical indication in 2012. Phan Thiet was once the largest fish sauce center in the South during the French colonial period.

cau_hoi: The "wind farm fields" along the coast, with turbine towers planted right on the tidal flats, are most famous in the old Bac Lieu province. Why is this area suitable for wind power?
A: Flat coastline, consistent and strong monsoon winds
B: No wind, so turbines are durable
C: There are high mountains blocking the wind
D: There is snow cooling the turbines
giai_thich: The Bac Lieu wind power plant, built in 2013, is Vietnam's first nearshore wind power plant. The turbines are placed on the coastal tidal flats, where winds from the sea are unobstructed by trees or buildings. The sight of white turbines against the sea has become a tourist attraction. From 2025, Bac Lieu will merge with Ca Mau.

cau_hoi: Nha Trang Bay, along with Ha Long Bay and Lang Co Bay, is a member of which organization?
A: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
D: Club of the Most Beautiful Bays in the World
giai_thich: The club was established in 1997 in Berlin (Germany), consisting of beautiful bays with natural and cultural value. Ha Long Bay joined in 2003, Nha Trang Bay in 2003, and Lang Co Bay (Hue) in 2009. Nha Trang Bay has 19 large and small islands, with Hon Tre being the largest.

cau_hoi: The Saigon River flows through the center of Ho Chi Minh City and merges with which river before emptying into the sea in the Can Gio region?
giai_thich: The Saigon River and the Dong Nai River meet near the Red Light Cape (Nha Be), forming the Nha Be River, which then splits into several branches such as Long Tau and Soai Rap that flow into the sea. There is a folk saying: "Nha Be water flows in two directions, whoever goes to Gia Dinh, Dong Nai should go back." The Saigon Port was once the largest port in the South located by this river.

cau_hoi: In the high mountainous region of the North, what is the harmful effect of the phenomenon "frost" on cold, clear, windless nights?
C: Causes crops, vegetables, and grass for livestock to burn leaves and die
giai_thich: Frost consists of water droplets that freeze white like salt on leaves when the ground temperature drops below 0°C. Ice breaks leaf cells, causing leaves to wilt and turn black after melting. Frost often appears in Sa Pa, Moc Chau, and Mau Son, causing damage to tea, vegetables, and pastures. Farmers cover plants or water them early to reduce damage.

cau_hoi: Cua Tung, a beautiful beach in Quang Tri where the Ben Hai River flows into the sea, was praised by the French with which title?
giai_thich: Cua Tung beach has fine white sand, clear water, and red basalt cliffs to the south, as this area once had volcanic eruptions. Offshore is Con Co Island, also formed from a volcano. The title "Pearl of the Far East" is reserved for Saigon, while "City of a Thousand Flowers" refers to Da Lat.

cau_hoi: In the North and South, the rainy season mainly falls in summer. What about the central coastal region (such as Hue, Da Nang), when does the main rainy season occur?
A: Autumn – winter, from September to December
giai_thich: In summer, the southwest wind is blocked by the Truong Son range, so the Central region is dry and hot. By autumn – winter, the northeast monsoon blows over the sea bringing moisture, and when it meets the Truong Son range, it is pushed up, causing heavy rain on the eastern slopes. Coupled with storms and tropical depressions, Hue is one of the rainiest places in the country.

cau_hoi: Where is the name of the city Da Lat believed to originate from?
B: From the name of a French king
C: From the name of a flower species
D: From "Da Lach": the stream of the Lach people, a group of indigenous K'Ho
giai_thich: "Da" means water, stream, while Lach is the name of a group of people living around Lang Biang mountain for a long time. Later, the French also "humorously explained" the name Da Lat with the Latin phrase "Dat Aliis Laetitiam Aliis Temperiem", meaning "to this person joy, to that person coolness", and this phrase was once engraved on the city's emblem.

cau_hoi: The Nha Trang Oceanographic Institute, established in 1922, is famous for what?
A: Being the largest salt production facility
B: Being the oldest marine research institute in Southeast Asia, with a museum containing tens of thousands of marine specimen
D: Being the first place to raise performing dolphins
giai_thich: The institute researches marine organisms, currents, and the seabed of the East Sea. Its museum has a skeleton of a humpback whale about 18 m long, many fish tanks, turtles, live corals, and tens of thousands of preserved specimens. Scientists here contribute to establishing the Mun Island marine reserve and researching Vietnam's maritime sovereignty and seafood resources.

cau_hoi: Mount Cam (about 705 m) in An Giang, the highest mountain in the Mekong Delta, belongs to which mountain range?
giai_thich: In the vast delta region, the seven mountains in An Giang rise near the Cambodian border, known as That Son. Mount Cam is also called "Heavenly Forbidden Mountain" and is humorously referred to by locals as the "roof of the West". On the mountain, there is a large statue of Buddha Maitreya and a cooler climate than the delta. Nearby is Sam Mountain with the Ba Chua Xu temple, the largest festival in the West.

cau_hoi: The coastal city of Vung Tau, famous for the statue of Christ on Small Mountain, was called what during the French colonial period?
giai_thich: The Portuguese named this peninsula after Saint James, and later the French called it Cap Saint-Jacques. Vung Tau means "anchorage for ships", as it has a sheltered bay. From 2025, Vung Tau will belong to Ho Chi Minh City. Offshore Vung Tau are large oil and gas fields such as Bach Ho and Rong, where oil has been extracted since the 1980s.

cau_hoi: Ngoc Linh Mountain Peak (about 2,598 m), home to the famous Ngoc Linh ginseng, is the highest peak of which mountain range?
B: Southern Truong Son and Central Highlands
giai_thich: Ngoc Linh is located between the old Kon Tum province (now Quang Ngai) and the old Quang Nam province (now Da Nang). The peak is shrouded in clouds year-round, with dense primary forests, and is home to many rare species. Ngoc Linh is about 550 m lower than Fansipan. Thanks to Ngoc Linh, Da Nang city has mountains higher than 2,500 m.

cau_hoi: From 2025, which province will have the largest area in Vietnam?
giai_thich: The new Lam Dong province, which includes Lam Dong, Dak Nong, and Binh Thuan, covers about 24,000 km². Previously, Nghe An (about 16,500 km²) was the largest province in the country, and it still retains its boundaries. The new Lam Dong province includes the Lam Vien plateau, the Dak Nong volcanic plateau, and the coastline of Binh Thuan with Mui Ne and Phu Quy Island.

cau_hoi: In 2025, when Binh Thuan province merges into Lam Dong province, which island will Lam Dong gain?
giai_thich: Phu Quy is about 120 km from Phan Thiet, formed by volcanic activity. The island features Cao Cat mountain and pristine beaches, and was once a district island. In 2025, Phu Quy will become a special administrative region. Nearby, there is Hon Tro, where an underwater volcanic eruption occurred in 1923.

cau_hoi: What record does the Tan Vu - Lach Huyen Bridge in Hai Phong, inaugurated in 2017, hold in Vietnam?
B: The highest suspension bridge in the world
C: The longest sea bridge in Vietnam, approximately 5.4 km long
giai_thich: The bridge connects Dinh Vu Island with Cat Hai Island, leading to the Lach Huyen deep-water port, the gateway for large container ships from the North. Built over the sea, it must withstand waves, storms, and saltwater corrosion. On the bridge, drivers can enjoy views of the sea on both sides and migrating birds in the mudflats.

cau_hoi: How do meteorologists define 'severe cold' and 'harmful cold' in Vietnam?
A: Severe cold below 0°C; harmful cold below −10°C
B: Severe cold when it snows; harmful cold when there is frost
C: Severe cold when it rains; harmful cold when there is wind
D: Severe cold when the average daily temperature is 15°C or below; harmful cold when it is 13°C or below
giai_thich: These definitions use the average temperature for the entire day, not the coldest temperature. During harmful cold, livestock can die from the cold, young rice can be damaged, and preschool and elementary school students in the North are given a day off if the temperature drops below the specified level. Farmers cover their barns and feed livestock more during cold spells.

cau_hoi: Where was the highest recorded temperature in Vietnam (approximately 44.2°C, in 2023) measured?
giai_thich: On May 7, 2023, the Tuong Duong meteorological station recorded 44.2°C, breaking the previous record of 43.4°C in Huong Khe (Ha Tinh) in 2019. Tuong Duong is located in the Ca River valley and is strongly affected by the hot dry Lao wind. Surprisingly, the hottest place is not in the South near the equator but in the North Central region due to the foehn effect.

cau_hoi: Besides the Red River, which major river in the North originates from Vietnam (Dien Bien), flows into Laos, and then returns to Vietnam to empty into the sea in Thanh Hoa?
giai_thich: The Ma River is approximately 500 km long, with about 100 km flowing through Laos. The river flows through rugged mountainous areas before reaching the Thanh Hoa plain. The Ma River is mentioned in the poem 'Tay Tien' by Quang Dung: 'The Ma River is far away, Tay Tien oh!'. Downstream, the Ma River deposits sediment, forming the Thanh Hoa plain, the largest plain in Central Vietnam.

cau_hoi: Which direction do the Sesan and Srepok rivers in the Central Highlands flow?
B: Flow into a closed lake with no outlet
C: Eastward, emptying into the East Sea
D: Westward, into Cambodia and then into the Mekong River
giai_thich: The Central Highlands is located on the western slope of the Southern Truong Son range, with terrain gradually lowering to the west, causing many rivers to flow into Cambodia. These rivers have many waterfalls and have been built with numerous hydropower plants such as Yaly on the Sesan River and Buon Kuop on the Srepok River. The famous Dray Nur waterfall is located on the Srepok River.

cau_hoi: The starting point of Vietnam's coastline in the north is Mui Sa Vi, near the Mong Cai border gate. Which province does this cape belong to?
giai_thich: Mui Sa Vi is located in Tra Co, Mong Cai city, where there is a landmark marking the starting point of the S-shaped coastline. Tra Co beach is about 17 km long. There is a saying 'From Mui Sa Vi to Mui Ca Mau' to refer to the entire length of the country's coastline. Mong Cai borders Dong Hung city (China), separated by the Ka Long River.

cau_hoi: In 2018, the Hon Thom cable car in Phu Quoc was recognized by the Guinness World Records for what record?
A: The longest three-rope sea cable car in the world (approximately 7.9 km)
B: The oldest cable car in the world
C: The highest cable car in the world
D: A cable car powered by wind
giai_thich: The cable car connects An Thoi town with Hon Thom island, flying over many small islands in the An Thoi archipelago, taking about 15 minutes. From above, visitors can see the blue sea, boats, and fishing villages. Vietnam also has the Fansipan cable car, which was once recognized by Guinness for having the largest elevation difference between the departure and arrival stations in the world.

cau_hoi: The Nhat Tan Bridge in Hanoi has five towers connected by cables. What does the number five symbolize?
C: The five gates of ancient Hanoi
giai_thich: The Nhat Tan Bridge was inaugurated in 2015, with the main span approximately 1.5 km long, making it the largest continuous cable-stayed bridge in Vietnam, built with loans from Japan. At night, the bridge is illuminated in many colors. The bridge connects central Hanoi with Noi Bai airport, thus considered the 'gateway' of the capital when international guests arrive.

cau_hoi: Vietnam's first oil refinery, which began operations in 2009, is located in which economic zone?
giai_thich: Before the oil refinery was built, Vietnam exported crude oil and then had to import refined petroleum products. Dung Quat has a deep, sheltered bay, convenient for oil tankers to dock. The refinery processes crude oil into gasoline, diesel, and liquefied gas. Later, the Nghi Son oil refinery in Thanh Hoa began operations in 2018.
