giai_thich: The enormous amount of floodwater poured into the lagoon but could not escape to the sea in time through the Thuan An and Tu Hien entrances, so it tore through the thin sandbank at Hoa Duan, opening a new sea entrance and sweeping away many houses. The new entrance was later filled in by artificial structures. This phenomenon shows that lagoons and coastal sandbanks are always changing over time.

cau_hoi: "An Nam đại quốc họa đồ" published by Bishop Taberd in 1838 has what significance for Vietnam's sovereignty over its islands?
A: Clearly records the Paracel Islands with the note "Paracel seu Cát Vàng", belonging to An Nam territory
C: Is a tourist map of Hanoi
D: Is the first map depicting America
giai_thich: The map was prepared by French bishop Jean-Louis Taberd and printed along with a Latin-Vietnamese dictionary. On the map, the Paracel Islands are depicted off the Central coast with a Latin note "Paracel seu Cát Vàng" (Paracel or Cát Vàng). This is one of the important Western documents proving that Vietnam has managed the Paracel Islands for a long time.

cau_hoi: Which province of Vietnam has the most islands, accounting for more than half of the total number of coastal islands in the country?
giai_thich: Quang Ninh has about 2,000 islands, most of which are limestone islands in Ha Long Bay and Bai Tu Long Bay, along with large islands such as Van Don, Co To, and Quan Lan. Many limestone islands are uninhabited due to a lack of fresh water and arable land. Vietnam has nearly 3,000 coastal islands and two offshore archipelagos, Hoang Sa and Truong Sa.

cau_hoi: In the summer, when the southwest wind brings heavy rain to the Central Highlands, what is the weather like in the coastal region of Central South Vietnam on the eastern side of the Truong Son range?
B: Hot and dry, with little rain, as it is on the sheltered side of the wind
D: More rain than the Central Highlands
giai_thich: The Southern Truong Son range acts as a wind barrier. The western slope receives wind, so the Central Highlands has a lot of rain, while the eastern slope is sheltered from the wind, making the coast dry. Conversely, in autumn-winter, the northeast wind from the sea causes heavy rain in the coastal region, while the Central Highlands experiences dry season. The phenomenon of the two slopes having opposite rainy seasons is called the "opposition" of rainy and dry seasons between the Eastern and Western Truong Son.

cau_hoi: How does the annual temperature range (the difference between the hottest and coldest months) in Vietnam change from South to North?
giai_thich: In Ho Chi Minh City, the hottest and coldest months differ by only about 3 – 4°C, due to its proximity to the equator and lack of a cold winter. In Hanoi, the difference is about 12°C, due to the northeast monsoon in winter. In the northern mountainous regions, the range is even greater. Conversely, the average annual temperature increases from North to South.

cau_hoi: What is the significance of the "Blue Whale" gas field, discovered in 2011 off the coast of Central Vietnam?
A: Is a breeding ground for whales
C: Is one of the largest natural gas fields discovered in Vietnam, offshore of old Quang Nam
giai_thich: The field was discovered by ExxonMobil (USA) in cooperation with Vietnam, with gas reserves of about 150 billion m³. The gas from the field is expected to be brought ashore to run gas power plants in Central Vietnam. However, the gas here contains many impurities of CO2, requiring complex treatment technology, so the development project is slow.

cau_hoi: In what year was the land border between Vietnam and China completed with demarcation and landmark placement on the ground?
giai_thich: The two countries signed the land border treaty in 1999. After nearly 10 years of work on the ground, on December 31, 2008, the demarcation and landmark placement was completed with nearly 2,000 markers. In 2009, legal documents were signed. This helped clarify and stabilize the border, facilitating trade at border gates.

cau_hoi: What does the name Pha Đin Pass, one of the "Four Great Passes" connecting Sơn La with Điện Biên, mean in Thai?
giai_thich: "Phạ" means heaven, "Đin" means earth, because the pass is so high that it seems to connect heaven and earth. The pass is about 32 km long, with many hairpin turns. In 1954, tens of thousands of workers used bicycles to transport rice over Pha Đin Pass to the battlefield of Điện Biên Phủ while French planes bombed day and night. Today, a new road has been built to avoid the dangerous old pass.

cau_hoi: How do geologists describe the limestone topography of Ha Long Bay using the two characteristic types "fengcong" and "fenglin"? How do these two types differ?
A: Fengcong is underwater, fenglin is above the clouds
B: The two terms refer to the same type of granite
C: Fengcong refers to limestone peaks with a common base, growing in clusters; fenglin refers to individual limestone towers like a forest of columns
D: Fengcong is a volcano, fenglin is a glacier
giai_thich: These are Chinese terms describing tropical karst. Ha Long Bay was recognized by UNESCO for the second time in 2000 due to its geological and geomorphological value, as it is a perfect example of submerged fengcong and fenglin karst, creating a unique "forest of islands". Caves like Sung Sot are traces of ancient groundwater levels.

cau_hoi: In many regions of the Red River Delta, well water can be contaminated with a natural toxin from sediments, causing illness if consumed over a long period. What is that substance?
giai_thich: Arsenic is present in the alluvial sediments of the Red River. Under conditions of low oxygen in groundwater, arsenic dissolves into the water. Arsenic-contaminated water is colorless and odorless, making it difficult for people to detect, but long-term consumption can cause skin diseases and cancer. Therefore, it is necessary to test well water, use sand filters, or switch to tap water.

cau_hoi: Why is the Tam Dao mountain range (north of Hanoi) named as such?
A: There are three peaks rising above the sea of clouds like three islands: Thach Ban, Thien Thi, and Phu Nghia
B: Because there are three islands in the sea
giai_thich: The three peaks are about 1,300 – 1,400 m high, often rising above the sea of clouds in winter, resembling three islands. Tam Dao is where the arc-shaped mountain ranges of the Northeast converge. Tam Dao National Park is home to many endemic species such as the Tam Dao frog. The Tam Dao resort town was built by the French in 1904.

cau_hoi: Where do scientists identify as the source most likely to cause tsunamis that could strongly affect the Central Vietnam coastline?
D: Manila Trench subduction zone, west of the Philippines
giai_thich: The Manila Trench is where the East Sea plate subducts beneath the Philippine plate. If a very large earthquake occurs here, a tsunami could propagate across the East Sea and reach the Central Vietnam coastline in about 2 hours. Therefore, Vietnam has installed tsunami warning stations along the coast. Historically, Vietnam has rarely suffered damage from tsunamis, but scientists remain vigilant.

cau_hoi: The old town of Muong Lay (Dien Bien) had to relocate its entire central area to higher ground around 2010. What was the reason?
C: The water level of Son La hydroelectric reservoir rising flooded the town area
giai_thich: Muong Lay (formerly Lai Chau) is located where the Nam Na River flows into the Da River. When the Son La reservoir filled, most of the old town was submerged. Residents were moved to resettlement areas on the hillside. Today, some rooftops and old bridges occasionally emerge when the water level of the reservoir drops in the dry season.

cau_hoi: In many place names in the South and Central South such as Cu Lao Cham, Cu Lao Re, Cu Lao Ong Ho, what does "cu lao" mean and where is it believed to originate from?
B: Means island (in the sea or in the river), derived from "pulau" in Malay – Cham
giai_thich: The Cham and Malay people both belong to the Austronesian language group, in which "pulau" means island. When the Vietnamese moved southward, they adopted this term as "cu lao". In the Mekong Delta, cu lao often refers to land areas between the Tien River and Hau River formed by alluvial deposits, such as Cu Lao Ong Ho (An Giang), Cu Lao Thoi Son. The name Con Dao during the French colonial period was Poulo Condore, which also originates from "pulau".
